questions.title: How much resource pack?
questions.context: The old pack is going away. A new one can only repaint item icons and, if you want, give every chest window one new background. Everything works without it.

options.label: Icons first, background later
options.detail: We start with about 55 repainted icons (under 100 KB). You decide on a background after you have seen them in game.

options.label: Icons and one background now
options.detail: Same icons plus one new chest-window look. It shows on every chest screen, real chests too, and you must draw it and keep text readable on it.

options.label: No pack at all
options.detail: Pure vanilla for good: nothing to download, nothing to draw, nothing to test on Bedrock.

questions.title: Should the pack be forced?
questions.context: Before, you wanted a forced pack with a prompt before joining. With only icons, every menu works the same without it, and nothing important is hidden.

options.label: Optional offer
options.detail: A short prompt; nobody is kicked for saying no, and players can get it later with /pack. This reverses the old answers 33 and 77.

options.label: Forced, as before
options.detail: Players who decline cannot join and are shown how to turn it on. Everyone sees the same icons, but some players will leave.

options.label: Optional now, forced at launch
options.detail: Test with real players first, then require it when the server opens.

questions.title: Remove the old pack now?
questions.context: The old pack changes menu titles, rank badges, icons, crate models and sounds. Removing it first shows how the game looks on plain vanilla.

options.label: Remove it all now
options.detail: Run pure vanilla until the new icons exist. Ranks show as plain coloured [Name] text and crates stay normal blocks.

options.label: Keep it until the new one is ready
options.detail: Two systems live side by side for weeks, with the old fonts and badges.

options.label: Remove all but the crate chests
options.detail: Crates keep their 3D chests and keys; everything else goes.

questions.title: Menu size and empty slots
questions.context: Chest windows are always 9 slots wide, but they can have fewer rows. Today every menu has a dark border with red corners.

options.label: Compact, empty slots stay empty
options.detail: 3, 4 or 6 rows depending on the content, buttons centred with gaps. No border and no filler panes.

options.label: Compact, quiet grey panes
options.detail: Same sizes, but empty slots in small menus get a plain grey pane so the window looks filled.

options.label: Keep today's frame
options.detail: Every menu keeps 6 rows with the black border and red corners. Safe, but busy.

questions.title: The bottom row of every menu
questions.context: Every menu shows the same buttons in the same places. Today: Back, ?, Close, Main menu and page arrows. MC Hub only has arrow, search, arrow.

options.label: Keep ours and add Search
options.detail: Back on the left, ? Close and Main menu in the middle, page arrows on the right, and a Search button next to the arrows on long lists.

options.label: MC Hub minimal row
options.detail: Only Back, Search and page arrows. Esc closes the menu; help comes from NPCs and the menu star.

options.label: Same as ours, but no Close
options.detail: Esc closes on Java and Bedrock has its own X, so the barrier button goes away.

questions.title: How names in menus look
questions.context: A button name can be plain or in brackets, and it can be coloured by what the button does.

options.label: Plain bold names, colour by meaning
options.detail: Green for money, gold for rewards, violet for skills, lime for island, aqua for the Depths, red only for danger. A yellow '» CLICK to open' line under each.

options.label: Bracket names like MC Hub
options.detail: [Members] and [Island Menu] with '* Click to view *'. They look like the clickable buttons in chat, which can confuse.

options.label: One colour for all names
options.detail: Every name in flame orange. Simplest, but no colour hint about what a button does.

questions.title: Delete and reset buttons
questions.context: Things you cannot undo (delete island or profile, disband, leave, permanent ban) must be hard to hit by accident.

options.label: Red TNT in a corner, then confirm
options.detail: One red TNT tile far from the safe buttons. A click opens a confirm screen; things that can never be undone ask twice.

options.label: One confirm screen only
options.detail: Same red tile, but always a single confirm screen.

options.label: Type the name to confirm
options.detail: For island and profile delete you must type the name. Safest, but slow on phones.

questions.title: Right-click on a shop item
questions.context: Left click opens the buy page and shift-click buys a stack on Java (both built). Right-click is still free; MC Hub uses it to sell. Bedrock cannot right-click, so it can only ever be a shortcut.

options.label: Right-click sells one
options.detail: Sells one of that item from your inventory (shift: a stack) at the live sell price, only if the sell chest accepts it. The sell chest stays for bulk. Replaces the 'right-click buys a stack' idea in C5-Q1.

options.label: Right-click buys a stack
options.detail: Same as shift-click but easier. Selling stays only in the sell chest.

options.label: No right-click shortcut
options.detail: One plain click everywhere; shift-click still buys a stack on Java.

questions.title: Currency look in text and menus
questions.context: Money, crystals, shards and credits each need a colour, a text symbol that also shows on Bedrock, and an item to show in menus.

options.label: Colour, symbol, vanilla item
options.detail: $ green money, ◆ aqua crystals, ✧ pink shards, ✦ orange credits (the old gem star). Menu items: gold ingot, amethyst shard, prismarine shard, diamond.

options.label: Colour and word only
options.detail: '1,200 Credits' with no symbols. No Bedrock risk, but longer lines on the scoreboard.

options.label: Credits without a symbol
options.detail: Credits stay '120 Credits' while the other three keep symbols (today's rule).

questions.title: Search in long lists
questions.context: Long lists are slow to scan. A Search button asks for a word (chat on Java, a small text box on Bedrock) and shows the matches on one page.

options.label: Every list over 3 pages
options.detail: Shop, auction house, island browser, player lists, collection and warps get a Search button next to the page arrows.

options.label: Shop and auction house only
options.detail: The two biggest lists. Everything else uses tabs and filters.

options.label: No search
options.detail: Tabs and pick menus only.

questions.title: Shape of the /menu hub
questions.context: The hub that is built now has your head and 14 buttons in four rows: Play, Money, Power and More. Rewards shows how many things wait.

options.label: Keep the clean hub
options.detail: Your head and 14 buttons in 4 coloured rows. Features that are not built are hidden. Easy to learn.

options.label: Smart hub
options.detail: Adds Recent and Pinned rows and category buttons. More to learn and more to build.

options.label: Seven category buttons
options.detail: Island, Depths, Economy, Progress, Rewards, Community, Settings, each opening a small menu. Cleanest, but one more click for everything.

questions.title: How the scoreboard looks
questions.context: The scoreboard stays plain text with no custom font. MC Hub shows two sections, a thin progress line and a timer.

options.label: Two sections with progress and timer
options.detail: '| You' and one place section (Island, Depths ...), 3 rows each, 10 lines at most. A progress line and a timer appear only while something runs.

options.label: Two sections, no progress or timer
options.detail: Same shape, but only plain rows. Progress stays in the action bar and boss bars.

options.label: Keep today's boards
options.detail: Up to three sections and no progress or timer lines.

questions.title: Tutorial bar colour and text
questions.context: The tutorial bar at the top of the screen should show one instruction and one progress. Today it is red and its fill sometimes shows distance instead of progress.

options.label: Yellow bar, step and instruction
options.detail: 'Tutorial 3/11 · Plant 3 wheat'. The bar fills with steps done, never with distance. Red stays for events and bosses.

options.label: Keep the red bar
options.detail: Same text and fill rules but red, like boss and event bars.

options.label: Blue like MC Hub
options.detail: A calm blue bar that no event uses, but not a phoenix colour.

questions.title: Hologram and NPC names
questions.context: Spawn holograms and NPC labels should say one title, one action and 'Click me'. MC Hub puts the NPC name in brackets with its command.

options.label: Bracket NPC names, command, Click me
options.detail: '[ Banker ]' then '/bank' then 'Click me'. Holograms: bold yellow title, white lines, 'Click me' only on clickable ones.

options.label: Names without brackets
options.detail: 'Banker' then 'Click', as today, with the same yellow titles and white lines for holograms.

options.label: Title only
options.detail: No command hint and no 'Click me' line; just a bold yellow name.

questions.title: Ranks and event tags in chat
questions.context: Colour makes chat easy to read. The old pack drew rank badges with a custom font; that is gone, so ranks are plain coloured text.

options.label: Coloured [RANK] words and event tags
options.detail: '[MOD] Pouched' in the rank colour, every rank a different colour. Server event lines start with a tag: [Crate], [Store], [Market], [Event], [Booster].

options.label: Rank words, no event tags
options.detail: Only the rank colours; event lines stay plain sentences.

options.label: Small symbols instead of words
options.detail: A symbol per rank instead of [MOD]. Shorter, but players must learn them and Bedrock shows few symbols.

questions.title: What do you draw first?
questions.context: You draw all the icons. Starting small shows quickly whether the pipeline and the look work, before you draw 50 more.

options.label: Tiny first slice: 5 icons
options.detail: Menu star and the 4 currencies. We check them on Java and Bedrock, then do the hub, buttons and shop tabs.

options.label: Hub first: about 45 icons
options.detail: Menu star, currencies, all hub, You and Travel icons and the navigation buttons in one go.

options.label: Own items first
options.detail: Crate keys and tool tiers, because they have no vanilla look. The rest waits.
